units.text: INT. CATHEDRAL BELL TOWER - DAY
Stone steps spiral up into a chamber of oak beams and ancient dust.
Light falls through louvered slits in thin gold bars.
In the center, a bronze bell the size of a truck, tongue wrapped in canvas.
SERGEANT IRENE VASCONCELOS (30s, face smeared with soot, helmet netted with dry grass) lies prone at a slit window, rifle braced, a cold cup of tea beside her elbow.
Below, a ruined square lies empty under the sun.
PRIVATE HAMZA QURESHI (19, spotter, binoculars on a strap) kneels at the next slit, lips moving silently as he counts windows across the plaza.
CORPORAL OTTOLINE DE WILDE (40s, radio operator, a darned sock peeking from her boot) sits against the bell with the handset in her lap.
She is knitting something small and gray.
Nobody speaks for a long time.
Down in the square, a dog crosses, trots, stops, sniffs a boot.
Hamza lowers his binoculars.
Irene does not move.
Was a good dog, once.
units.name: OTTOLINE

units.text: Mm.
units.name: IRENE

units.text: The dog moves on.
Hamza lifts the glasses.
Ottoline's needles click.
The bell ticks softly as the stone cools.
Four minutes.
units.name: HAMZA

units.text: Irene breathes out, slowly, and in.
She touches the cold tea with one finger, not drinking it.
